critical_code_review_comments: server.py (~586): enable_share reuses existing token on subsequent calls — this is the tested/expected behavior, but is subtle. Consider documenting: users must call /share/rotate to invalidate a leaked token.

public_map (line ~624) projects out {user_id, file_id, point_overrides}, and then re-shapes into a fresh dict — good defense-in-depth. status_column is returned both at top-level AND inside map — mild duplication but harmless.

MapUpdate.header_row/first_col are `Optional[int]` with no validation — sending 0 or negative would be accepted and persisted. _parse_sheet clamps with max(1, ...) so it won't crash, but consider Pydantic Field(ge=1) for cleaner API contract.

MapUpdate.status_column: sending empty string '' would persist and then in _build_map_rows the condition `if status_col and status_col in headers` would be falsy, so status filtering is silently disabled. Consider trimming/None-ifying.
cached_rows can grow large (embedded in map doc). If Excel has thousands of rows, doc size may approach Mongo's 16MB limit. Consider a separate collection or trimming/paging.
share_token uses uuid4().hex (128 bits) — cryptographically fine. Consider using secrets.token_hex(16) for explicit intent (equivalent entropy).
server.py is now ~670 lines. Splitting into routers (auth / maps / share / onedrive) recommended before adding more features.
No rate-limiting on GET /api/public/maps/{token} — a leaked/guessed token has no throttling. Consider adding basic per-IP rate limit for the public endpoint.
test_credentials: None used. Two TEST_ sessions/users (A + B) injected directly into MongoDB; all maps carry TEST_ user_id prefix.
seed_data_creation: Module-scoped fixtures create session_a and session_b (both TEST_ prefixed). All maps created belong to these test users. Fixtures teardown deletes sessions + maps by user_id. Post-run verification: 0 TEST_ sessions / 0 TEST_ maps remain.
